subject: Request: territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot
messages:
From: Darren Lee <darren.lee@cortexlabs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cortexlabs.com
Date: 2026-10-19T15:22:00Z
Subject: Territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — Cortex is excited to move the pilot forward. As part of our security intake we need a short attestation confirming that for the EU pilot traffic and persistent storage will remain within EU-hosted infrastructure and that private connectivity (Privatelink/Peering) will not egress through the US.

Specifically can you provide: 
- A one-page attestation (signed or stamped) confirming EU-only hosting for the DL-4728 pilot.
- A network topology diagram that shows the peered path for Privatelink (including where KEKs/KMS are located).
- A mapping of SOC 2 controls / SIG answers that are relevant to data residency (if a full SIG is heavy, a control mapping PDF is fine).
- Any runbook snippets that describe how fallback to public endpoints is prevented during maintenance windows.

Our timeline is tight — we need the packet by EOD Thursday (2026-10-22) to proceed with procurement. Let me know if you need an NDA or any other intake form.

Thanks,
Darren
Director, Security & Infrastructure
Cortex Labs
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Darren Lee <darren.lee@cortexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot

Hi Darren — thanks for the clear list. Glad the demo was useful.

Short answers up front: yes, we can provide an EU-only hosting attestation and the peered network diagram; we will also include a SOC 2 -> SIG control mapping that highlights residency-related controls. We will not route pilot data through US egress for the requested EU-only pilot configuration.

What I will attach in the packet:
- redwood-soc2-sig-mapping.pdf (control mapping + references to SOC 2 sections relevant to data locality)
- privatelink-topology-v2.png (peering diagram, annotated with KMS/region labels)
- onboarding-runbook-privatedeploy.md (snippet with maintenance/fallback procedures and guardrails)

A couple of clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need:
1) Is the requirement strictly EU 27 (including UK) or EU mainland only? We can call out specific AZs/regions in the attestation if you need finer granularity.
2) For KMS, do you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) referenced in the attestation or is provider-managed KMS acceptable as long as keys are region-bound?
3) Would a short signed letter from our Security leadership be sufficient for procurement, or do you need notarization?

Target: we will circulate the initial evidence packet tomorrow EOD (2026-10-20) internally and aim to send you the finalized packet by 2026-10-21 morning for your review. If that matches your procurement timeline we should be good.

Attaching a lightweight draft mapping for your preview — will follow up with full artifacts.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: draft-mapping-snippet.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T13:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot

Forwarding to ops for a quick sanity check on topology and KMS placement.

-- Forwarded message --
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Darren Lee <darren.lee@cortexlabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot

Olga: two quick technical notes below —
1) For EU-only pilot we should pin to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 nodes; avoid edge egress to us-east unless the customer explicitly opts into cross-region DR.
2) Privatelink termination points will be in EU peering locations; KMS key material will be kept in the customer-specified EU key store when CMK is enabled. If CMK is not enabled, provider-managed keys are still region-bound and not replicated outside EU.

I will attach a sanitized topology diagram and the runbook excerpt for admission into the packet (privatelink-topology-v2.png, onboarding-runbook-privatedeploy.md).

Karthik
Head of Infrastructure
From: Darren Lee <darren.lee@cortexlabs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cortexlabs.com
Date: 2026-10-21T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Territorial hosting attestation & peered-network diagram for Cortex pilot

Olga, Karthik — this looks great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Two small follow-ups: 
- For the attestation, EU mainland (no-UK) is the requirement — could you call out eu-central-1 as the canonical region in the letter?
- For the KMS note, Cortex will leverage our CMK; please include the short snippet that shows customer-held CMK is supported and that key material is not exported.

If you can slide those two clarifications into the attestation, procurement can sign off on Friday. We also want a 30-minute sync to close out the packet — is Friday 10:00 UTC open?

I appreciate the responsive team.

Best,
Darren
Director, Security & Infrastructure
Cortex Labs
Attachments: cortex-intake-form.pdf
